before: require_relative resolves a path relative to the file containing the call, not the process working directory. It loads a feature once and does not re-execute it for the repeated same feature request. This is code execution, so never derive the path directly from untrusted input.

Save this as helper.rb beside main.rb:
```ruby
puts "loaded"
module StudyHelper
  def self.label
    "ready"
  end
end
```
The main example requires it twice. load, in contrast, executes a file again on each call; it also has different path-handling rules, so it is not a drop-in caching switch.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:

Read helper.rb. It prints loaded and defines the method used by the main file.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
# File: helper.rb
puts "loaded"
module StudyHelper
  def self.label
    "ready"
  end
end

# File: main.rb
require_relative "helper"
require_relative "helper"
puts StudyHelper.label
```
The output is `loaded`, then `ready`. The helper runs once; calling its method later gives ready.
